summary: The manuscript resolves three open analytical and algorithmic gaps in the Dicke-state AQMBS preparation framework of Asari, Kunimi, and Nikuni [1]. Theorem A derives exact without-replacement fourth and sixth Dicke-state moments across all four cosine-sum resonance branches, establishing universal sharp bounds kappa_4 <= 3 (equality iff (M',n,l)=(4,2,2)), kappa_6 < 15, and kappa_6 - kappa_4^2 < 6. Theorem B optimizes the linear projection in block-encoded infidelity estimation to obtain a uniform non-asymptotic infidelity bound, improving bare p_succ by 37.94x and certifying zero-overshoot single-round Grover amplification p_amp^(1) >= 0.94488 at s=0.495 (and 1-F < 0.01 uniformly at s=0.45). Theorem C constructs a collision-free MSB-to-LSB reversible router unifying Onsager and DWC maps using O(M log^2 n) 3-qubit gates and O(M log n) clean ancillas, beating pruned sitewise-displacement conveyors permanently for M' >= 184 (Stage-2) and M' >= 382 (total 3-qubit gates) at half filling. All proofs and standalone Appendix A tables are internally consistent with no material objections.
weaknesses: Theorem C achieves subquadratic gate complexity at the expense of O(M log n) clean ancillas (LB shift ancillas plus 2B counter/carry ancillas) and Omega(M) sequential circuit depth, making the gate advantage primarily relevant to fault-tolerant extensive-filling regimes (M' >= 382 at half filling) rather than small NISQ chains (as noted in Remark 1).

Theorem B certifies 1 - F < 0.01 uniformly at s = 0.45 (where 1 - F <= 0.009746) rather than at [1]'s operating point s = 0.495 (where 1 - F <= 0.015383, consistent with the Gaussian limit already slightly exceeding 0.01).

The formalization covers the algebraic integer/natural-number cores in Lean 4.35.0 and exact rational replay in Python, leaving the two real-analytic Taylor bounds in Theorem B and the general-M' quantum circuit proof of Theorem C as analytical paper proofs.
